cards.definition: The written record of what was said and decided in a meeting.
cards.example:
- Could you send the minutes to everyone after the call?
Você poderia mandar a ata para todos depois da reunião?
cards.note: Nesse sentido é sempre plural. Take the minutes = fazer a ata.

cards.definition: A person who is present at a meeting or event.
cards.example:
- There were twelve attendees, but only four of them spoke.
Havia doze participantes, mas só quatro deles falaram.
cards.note: De attend. O sufixo -ee marca quem recebe a ação: employee, interviewee, trainee.

cards.definition: To finish something, especially a meeting.
cards.example:
- Let's wrap up — we're already two minutes over.
Vamos encerrar — já estamos dois minutos além do tempo.
cards.note: Muito comum e nada rude. Substantivo: a quick wrap-up = um fechamento rápido.

cards.definition: To review or check something again.
cards.example:
- Can we go over the numbers one more time before we vote?
Podemos revisar os números mais uma vez antes de votar?
cards.note: Go over = revisar por cima; go through = percorrer item por item.

cards.definition: To mention a subject so people can talk about it.
cards.example:
- She brought up a good point about the budget.
Ela levantou um bom ponto sobre o orçamento.
cards.note: Separável: bring it up. Quem levanta o ponto certo é lembrado depois.

cards.definition: For a short time, using few words.
cards.example:
- Can I comment briefly on the second item?
Posso comentar brevemente o segundo item?
cards.note: Pedir espaço com briefly quase nunca é negado — você está prometendo ser curto.

cards.definition: A polite way of asking to interrupt and speak.
cards.example:
- Sorry — can I jump in here for a second?
Desculpe — posso entrar aqui por um segundo?
cards.note: A forma educada de interromper em inglês. Alternativa: Can I add something?

cards.definition: Used to suggest going to the next subject.
cards.example:
- Good point. Let's move on to the next item.
Bom ponto. Vamos seguir para o próximo item.
cards.note: Fecha um assunto sem soar rude. Suaviza ainda mais com for now: let's move on for now.

cards.definition: The list of subjects to be discussed in a meeting.
cards.example:
- The agenda has four items and we're still on the first one.
A pauta tem quatro itens e ainda estamos no primeiro.
cards.note: “Agenda” de anotar compromissos é planner, diary ou calendar. Agenda = a pauta.

cards.definition: To expect something and prepare for it.
cards.example:
- We anticipate some resistance from the client.
Prevemos alguma resistência do cliente.
cards.note: “Antecipar a reunião” NÃO é anticipate — é move the meeting up.

questions.prompt: Someone writes down the decisions of the meeting. They…
questions.explanation: You TAKE minutes. “Fazer a ata” tempts “make”.

questions.prompt: There were twelve _____, but only four of them spoke.
questions.explanation: An “attendee” is someone present; the plural takes -s.

questions.prompt: The meeting is running over. You say:
You want to review the numbers once more. You say:
questions.explanation: “Go over” does NOT split — compare with “bring up”, which does.

questions.prompt: She mentioned the budget in the meeting. She…
questions.explanation: “Bring up” splits with a pronoun. Two phrasal verbs, opposite rules.

questions.prompt: Can I comment _____ on the second item?
_____ I think we are missing one number here.
questions.explanation: A polite way of interrupting in a meeting.

questions.prompt: We have decided that one — _____ to the next item.
Você pode mandar a pauta antes da reunião?
questions.answer: Could you send the agenda before the meeting?|Can you send the agenda before the meeting?
questions.explanation: “Agenda” is the list of subjects. Your personal diary is a “schedule” or “calendar”.

questions.prompt: We expected the delay and prepared for it. We…
questions.explanation: “Anticipate” is to foresee. It does not mean to bring a date forward — that is “move up” or “bring forward”.
